blocks.heading: Where could Walmart Inc.'s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $112.05 in October 2027, a 2% return with dividends. The October 2028 weighted price is $112.96, a 4% return. The October 2029 figure is $114.26, a 6% return. The 2029 range is $77.23 to $171.09. Today’s price is $110.56.
The base case receives a 60% probability. The bear case receives 25%, and the bull case 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Walmart Inc.?

paragraphs.text: The bear case starts at $24,700m and reaches $25,421m. It assumes about 3% annual revenue growth from the $736bn base, with margins falling from 3.25% to 3.15%. The bull case spans $27,584m to $33,174m, supported by stronger transactions, digital demand, advertising, membership and fulfillment productivity. The base is supported by guidance for 4–5% sales growth and faster operating-income growth, plus seven earnings beats in eight reports. The forecast removes tariff refunds and other identified one-time items, so the bull requires recurring improvement.

The bull case reaches $133.22 first and $171.09 last. Its 15% probability reflects the need for transaction growth, lower fulfillment costs, stronger advertising and membership profits, and recurring cash generation to succeed together. The evidence shows growth in these businesses, but not yet their complete profit economics.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Walmart Inc. really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock-based compensation saves current cash but gives employees a claim on the business. Deducting it is a conservative way to estimate what remains for existing shareholders, even though it is not a second cash payment. Its share of revenue increased across the period.

dividend.opening: Walmart has approved a $0.99 annual dividend rate and has raised it for 53 consecutive years. The dividend is tested against free cash flow after stock pay, while shareholder distributions can exceed internally generated cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Walmart’s business, compares its rivals, examines management’s plans, and lays out the risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Walmart Inc. pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise moderately because Walmart has approved a $0.99 annual rate and has raised its dividend for 53 consecutive years. The base reaches $1.15 by 2029 through roughly 5% annual increases. The bear holds near $0.99 before reaching $1.00, while the bull reaches $1.23 through roughly 7% increases. High capital spending and first-half free cash flow of $5.529bn argue for restraint.

blocks.heading: Is Walmart Inc.'s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow means the cash left after operating needs and property-and-equipment spending. Stock compensation reduces the economic amount available to existing owners because employees receive part of the company, even when no cash leaves immediately. The table therefore tests whether dividends and repurchases were covered by cash after both investment and that ownership cost.

Shareholder distributions can exceed internally generated cash, with disposal proceeds, cash balances or borrowing filling the gap. Buybacks create value only when Walmart pays less than the value of the shares it retires. The central capital question is therefore whether operating savings will catch up with the rising investment bill before distributions limit Walmart’s flexibility.

blocks.heading: What could change Walmart Inc.'s dividend?

paragraphs.text: The forecast would move toward the bear case during FY2027–FY2028 if U.S. comparable sales and transactions slow below expectations. From FY2027 through FY2029, fading tariff refunds, high capital spending and rising depreciation would weaken margins and make buybacks less affordable.

The bull case would gain credibility during FY2027–FY2029 if reliable availability sustains unit growth, order density and automation reduce fulfillment costs, and advertising and membership add recurring profit. From FY2028 onward, stronger cash generation would need to fund both investment and faster buybacks.

blocks.heading: What has Walmart Inc. guided for FY2027?

paragraphs.text: Walmart’s share price could reach $114.26 by October 2029, but that outcome hinges on earnings growth and Walmart sustaining a premium valuation. Management guides to 4–5% net sales growth and 7–8.5% adjusted operating-income growth at constant currency for FY2027. It guides to adjusted EPS of $2.80–$2.87 and capital expenditure of 4.0% of sales.

blocks.heading: Has Walmart Inc. kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management promised profit growth faster than sales. Fiscal 2026 adjusted profit grew 5.4% against constant-currency revenue growth of 5.1%, narrowly meeting that direction. Later guidance raised planned capital spending to about 4.0% of sales, so the next test is whether greater investment produces the returns used to justify pay.

blocks.heading: How have Walmart Inc. revenue and profit changed?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 5.9%, while operating income rose 28.8%. Net income and diluted EPS nevertheless fell. The quarter separates the retail engine from the items below it.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Walmart Inc.'s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results will test whether Walmart’s investment is producing recurring gains. The November 19, 2026 report covers the October quarter, while the February 18, 2027 report covers the January year-end. November should show how lower prices affect profit after tariff refunds; February should show whether Flipkart’s shifted event produces the expected holiday benefit. Across both reports, transactions, cash after investment and productivity after depreciation matter more than a single earnings headline.
